headline: Japan's Fujitsu agreed with the state of New Mexico to set up a quantum computing research center there.
score_reason: Official announcement of a new research center by a major company, but no money, date or hiring figures are given.
importance_line: It brings a major foreign technology firm into a state that already hosts national laboratories and several quantum companies, with training programmes promised for local people, but the announcement gives no investment figure, opening date or hiring numbers.
source: Office of the Governor of New Mexico
summary: New Mexico's governor announced that Fujitsu, the Tokyo-based technology group, will set up a research center in the state covering quantum hardware, software and algorithms, with education and workforce programmes and planned work with the University of New Mexico's Quantum New Mexico Institute. The deal follows the governor's trade missions to Japan and builds on a 2025 research agreement between Fujitsu and New Mexico State University.
notes: Original is the governor's office release (HPCwire carries it as an off-the-wire item and was blocked, HTTP 403); link points to the governor's page where the text was read.
